newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cobepa rises on interview, stock picking.
newsitem.headline: Cobepa rises on interview, stock picking.

text.p: Belgian investment firm Cie. Benelux Paribas (Cobepa) rose strongly on the Brussels bourse on Monday on the back of a weekend newspaper interview with its chief executive officer and as investors sought opportunities in a strong market, dealers said.
By around 1000 GMT, Cobepa was up 44 francs, or 3.8 percent, at 1,204 francs, making it the leading share on the Brussels Stock Exchange. Volume was an above average 19,108 shares.
"Even before the interview we had rated the share," said a trader at brokerage G-Securities. "It's net asset value was about 30 percent over its price, which is very wide."
Another trader said Cobepa, like other holdings, was beginning to be re-examined after lagging the strong rise in share prices of its units in recent weeks.

Cobepa CEO Pierre Scohier told La Libre Belgique newspaper at the weekend that Cobepa was studying various options for its 17.6 percent stake in Belgian retailing group GIB. GIB general retailing stores Sarma and Inno could be spun off or merged with other groups. It was also possible that GIB's French partner Promodes could enter the capital of GIB supermarket unit GB.
In a separate interview in L'Echo newspaper, GB also confirmed it would swing back into the black in 1996 after three difficult years of restructuring.
Scohier said in 1997 the turnaround would be even stronger.
"It's clear: the arrival of a partner within the framework of an industrial project is not excluded but there is no more restructuring in sight," he told La Libre.
Scohier also used the interview to highlight the performance of Cobepa interests in car distributor D'Ieteren and Cobepa's role in various Belgian insurance mergers this year.
